annotations.count_cue: 114 Surahs — the canonical Quran chapter count, INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED for this edition: each surah body opens with its name in ALL-CAPS followed by a '(Revealed before/after Hijrah)' line. A literal scan for '(Revealed' yields 111; the 3 misses are OCR-garbled descenders of the SAME marker (e.g. Al-Fatihah's '(Revealed hefi,r; l fiirah)', Al-A'raf's '(Revealed be/iJre Hijrah)') — walking the ALL-CAPS name line that precedes every such marker recovers all 114, AL-FATIHAH(1) … AN-NAS(114), matching the TOC's Chapter_1 … Chapter_114. NOTE: the CURRENT detector emits 925 'chapter' sections — it segments on the per-PAGE running head 'Chapter N - <arabic>' (≈925 pages), NOT on the 114 surah bodies, so its recall against this gold is >>1 (over-segmentation, not a miss). The surah is the true content chapter.

exemplars.note: Surah 1 (Al-Fatihah) — first surah; '(Revealed before Hijrah)' OCR-garbled to 'hefi,r; l fiirah'
Surah 2 (Al-Baqarah) — longest surah; '(Revealed after Hijrah)' garbled to 'after l fiirah'
Surah 114 (An-Nas) — last surah; the marker mis-OCR'd 'after' (canonically Revealed before Hijrah)

annotations.note: PRIMARY content structure. The 114 surahs are the navigational chapters; verses within are the (masked) body. Type=chapter (UNMASKED) per taxonomy. The English verse text + footnote apparatus is interleaved within each surah.

annotations.count_cue: 30 Juz' (Parts) — the canonical 30-fold liturgical division of the Quran, cross-checked against the front-matter 'List of Parts with Page Numbers' which enumerates Part 1 (p.1) … Part 30 (p.889). Parts are ORTHOGONAL to surahs (a Juz' boundary falls MID-surah: 'Part 2' begins inside AL-BAQARAH), so this is a secondary overlay grouping, not a container of chapters nor contained by them. In-body Part boundaries are signalled only by per-page running heads 'Part N - <arabic>', whose numerals are OCR-noisy (I/1, II/11, and parts 6,7,19 lost to garble — 29 distinct tokens recovered of 30), so per-instance anchoring of Part STARTS is unreliable; the 30 count is established from the clean TOC list, exemplar-anchored there.

HIGH-VALUE LAYER. The entire scripture body is Maulawi Sher Ali's English TRANSLATION of the Quran (numbered verses, e.g. '1. In the name of Allah, the Gracious, the Merciful.'). Span runs from Surah 1 to the back-matter 'Prayer offered at the completion of the recitation'. SCOPING CAVEAT (honest, required): the PDF text layer renders the original ARABIC as garbage glyphs (e.g. 'r ;;.iµ,', '~ J' ~', the recurring 'a i u I / I th .::,' transliteration-key debris on every page) because the embedded font's glyph→Unicode map is broken. ONLY the English translation + Latin structure extract cleanly; Arabic verse text is NOT annotated here and OCR of it is DEFERRED. This single span therefore covers the clean translation layer that is interleaved (per detector) with 925 page-chapter/header segments.

annotations.count_cue: Per-verse explanatory commentary apparatus — Sher Ali's translator notes plus Hazrat Mirza Tahir Ahmad's alternative-translation notes (Foreword: bold alternatives + footnotes marked with starlets '*', dagger 't'/'‡' for the translator's own notes, '(publisher)' tag for publisher notes). Discrete prose 'Note:' annotations occur 48× (line-anchored), and per-verse footnote starlets appear ~1700×; daggered footnote bodies (e.g. 't I am Allah, the All-Knowing.') RECUR across pages so most footnote text is NOT uniquely exemplar-anchorable, hence expected_count=null (presence layer). Count is left null deliberately rather than guessing — the apparatus is densely interleaved with the translation and OCR-fragmented.
